headline: U.S. Job Growth Beats Expectations in October as Labor Concerns Persist
summary: The U.S. economy added more jobs than expected in October, though underlying labor market weaknesses and persistent inflation continued.
why: Employment figures are a primary indicator monitored by the Federal Reserve and financial markets to gauge economic health and dictate monetary policy.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Stronger-than-expected job growth influences Federal Reserve interest rate expectations, directly impacting equity valuations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Better-than-expected job growth beats expectations, but underlying labor market weaknesses and persistent inflation keep concerns alive regarding future Federal Reserve policy.
